differential:heap-destroy.scope: Pinned-C/Rust main-Heap Theap-list destruction after process_done retained worker TLDs (M2 building block of Heap and subprocess destruction).

differential:arena-destroy.scope: Pinned-C/Rust quiescent arena-group retirement with regular, external, and huge owners and failed-release retries (M2 building block of subprocess destruction).

differential:public-heap-lifecycle.scope: Pinned-C/Rust traces of non-main Heaps on a child-subprocess thread: mi_heap_new list push order and links, Heap sequence numbers, dynamic thread-local keys and their index reuse, Heap counts and heaps statistics, main-Heap delete/destroy refusal, delete/destroy of Heaps that never allocate, the per-thread Theap a first mi_heap_malloc creates (TLD and Heap list position, dynamic thread-local slot, cached-Theap reference counts moved by the nested per-arena page-record allocation, theaps statistics, arena page records), local frees, mi_heap_destroy with live pages (Theaps leave their TLDs; a cached Theap outlives its Heap until the next main-Heap allocation or thread finish), mi_heap_delete moving live pages to the main Heap as abandoned pages, non-main page abandonment at thread finish (arena and OS-backed pages), reclaim of abandoned child pages on free and on allocation, mi_subproc_destroy of a non-main Heap with an abandoned live page, and, on an ordinary thread of the process main subprocess, first-allocation Theap shapes, huge OS-backed pages moved by mi_heap_delete or released by mi_heap_destroy, and 1000 live Heaps growing the thread-local slot array. A source-built shared public driver additionally checks child mi_heap_main, mi_heap_new, mi_heap_theap, Heap visitation/list order, direct non-main Theap allocation and default substitution/restoration on one TLD, ownership, zeroing, cache preservation, oversized errno, delete/destroy, dynamic-key reuse source diagnostics, worker exit, and subprocess teardown.

differential:heap-in-arena.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter process-main mi_heap_new_in_arena with one live exclusive parent: Heap list membership, Theap and page placement, requested-arena allocation and OS-fallback refusal, live-page delete move, free/destroy and slice reuse, failed reservation output, null-ID ordinary policy, source Heap binding, and errno.

differential:child-heap-in-arena.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter child-subprocess mi_heap_new_in_arena with a live child-owned exclusive parent: Theap and page placement, requested-arena allocation and OS-fallback refusal, live-page delete move, free/destroy and subsequent selected allocation, failed reservation output, null-ID ordinary policy, source Heap and arena subprocess binding, and errno.

differential:public-heap-adapter.scope: Shared-driver pinned-C/native-adapter traces of the exported M6 entries: mi_reserve_os_memory and mi_reserve_os_memory_ex (committed, lazily committed, too-small, exclusive, failing, and over-limit reservations with their statistics and errno), mi_heap_new, mi_heap_main, the mi_heap_malloc/zalloc/calloc/mallocn/small and aligned[_at] allocation entries with their failure errors and messages, the mi_heap_realloc family (in-place reuse only within the block's own Heap, including from another thread), mi_realloc of a Heap block, mi_heap_strdup/strndup/realpath, mi_heap_alloc_new[_n], mi_heap_collect with its deferred-free callback and page release, Heap PageMap and quiescent utilization queries for null, foreign, interior, moved, and joined-remote-free non-head pages, main-Heap delete/destroy warnings, test-api.c heap-os1/heap-os2/heap-many with page and Heap statistics, a clean forked process-main Heap visitor traversing regular and OS singleton pages with live-block filtering and early stops, and a second thread allocating from a shared Heap, deleting its own, and finishing before the Heap is destroyed, and the subprocess entries: main and current ids, Heap visitation with an early stop, main-id add/destroy being ignored, the other-subprocess warning, a child whose thread allocates, creates, visits, and deletes a Heap and finishes, and destruction of that child with its statistics merged, and a child destroyed under a thread that still belongs to it, with its Heap, Theap, and thread statistics merged into main.

differential:public-heap-alignment.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter mi_heap_zalloc_aligned_at over ordinary and large alignments with offsets, zeroed client extents, invalid alignment and overflow errno, a worker-owned Theap, source Heap identity and a live OS-backed aligned block through mi_heap_delete and its final free, and mi_heap_destroy with a live aligned block.

differential:heap-delete-after-owner-exi.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter Heap created with regular and aligned OS-backed live pages on a worker; after that owner exits, another thread deletes the Heap, remotely frees both moved live blocks, and collects them while comparing Heap identity, PageMap membership, payload, and errno.

differential:heap-destroy-after-workers.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter Heap whose creating worker exits with a live page, whose second worker allocates regular and aligned pages after that exit, and whose main-thread destroy retires every live page after both workers exit; compare Heap identity, payload, PageMap membership, errno, and page/Theap statistics.

differential:heap-destroy-with-attached-.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter Heap destruction after its creator exits while a second worker retains a live Theap: the creator's page retires, the worker's regular and aligned pages remain registered, the cached Theap survives through worker exit, and errno and page/Theap statistics match.

differential:heap-delete-with-attached-w.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter Heap deletion after its creator exits while a second worker retains a live Theap: regular and aligned pages remain registered through the delete and joined worker, their final frees follow source page movement, and errno and page/Theap statistics match.

differential:heap-destroy-racing-detach.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter thirty-two independent 64-round races between non-main Heap destruction and the second worker's thread exit after the creating worker has exited: every creator page retires and Heap/Theap counts return to baseline.

differential:deleted-heap-remote-exit.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter deleted process-main Heap with an aligned OS-backed live block, remote final free before or after the owner exits, Heap and region identity, errno, collection, and page/Theap statistics.

differential:main-heap-visitor-populatio.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter main-Heap area and block population through live non-main Heap allocation, destruction, visitor remote collection, and final collection for 1, 2, 10, 100, 250, 500, and 1000 Heaps; includes direct/fork and reserved-arena cases, detached Theap-image frees, and replaced dynamic TLS slot images.

differential:main-population-after-owner.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter main-Heap area, live-block, page-class, and page-count traces after two worker owners exit with accumulated regular, medium, and aligned singleton allocations; compares Heap deletion, destruction, moved-page ownership, remote frees, collection, payload, errno, and final PageMap membership.

differential:abandoned-heap-visitor.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter mi_heap_visit_abandoned_blocks over one non-main Heap regular page abandoned after its allocating worker exits: area-before-block order, one freed and two live blocks, and area/block callback early stops.

differential:abandoned-os-heap-visitor.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter mi_heap_visit_abandoned_blocks over a worker Heap's OS singleton page after thread exit: the freed singleton is absent, the live singleton receives area-before-block callbacks, and both callback early stops preserve source results.

differential:abandoned-combined-heap-vis.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter mi_heap_visit_abandoned_blocks on one worker Heap with both a mapped abandoned regular page and an OS singleton after thread exit: regular bin before OS-list area/block order despite OS allocation first, freed regular block omission, and early stops within the regular page.

differential:main-abandoned-heap-visitor.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter mi_heap_visit_abandoned_blocks on the process main Heap after a worker's regular page enters its main-arena abandoned bitmap: exact selected bin membership with a separate non-abandoned same-size page, live/freed block filtering, area/block early stops, and null-Heap selection.

differential:main-abandoned-os-heap-visi.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter mi_heap_visit_abandoned_blocks on the process main Heap with a main-thread OS singleton and a later worker-abandoned OS singleton: source OS-list membership and order, freed worker page omission, area/block early stops, and null-Heap selection.

differential:main-abandoned-mixed-heap-v.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter process-main abandoned visitation over two worker regular bins and an OS singleton allocated in reverse traversal order, with separate live main-thread regular and OS pages: exact bitmap/list membership, bin-before-OS order, freed block/page omission, area/block early stops in each selected page, and null-Heap selection.

differential:public-theap.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter traces of mi_theap_get_default, mi_theap_set_default, mi_heap_theap, mi_theap_malloc, mi_theap_zalloc, and default-root mi_malloc across the process main thread, one worker, and a fork child: initialized candidate and null refusal, exact previous/default pointers, main and auxiliary Heap ownership, shared TLD, zeroing, restoration, and parent root preservation.

differential:public-arena.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter public arena reservation, caller-owned committed and reserved memory in main and child subprocesses, exclusive Heap selection, arena area and containment queries across workers, caller-retained backing and purge, and a 17 GiB external mapping split into parent and child arenas while one parent ID covers the full range.

differential:managed-os-lifecycle.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter public mi_manage_os_memory with caller-owned mapped areas in the process main and one child subprocess: nonexclusive external arena registration without an ID output, 64-byte allocation inside each managed area with automatic reservation disabled, exact short-region refusal warning and unchanged errno, child Heap deletion and thread exit, child subprocess destruction preserving the external mapping, and caller-held terminal munmap.

differential:managed-callback.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter public mi_manage_memory in the process main subprocess with caller-owned aligned memory: short-region refusal, null arena output, unchanged errno, and warning without callback; metadata and selected-allocation commit callback order, contained offsets and lengths, nullable zero output, two page purges after free and Heap destroy, retained mapping, and caller-held munmap immediately before process exit.

differential:managed-callback-failure.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter process-main mi_manage_memory with a callback that rejects its first metadata commit: null arena output, unchanged errno, one metadata warning, retained caller mapping, successful retry on that mapping, selected Heap allocation and release, one purge callback returning no-recommit without unmapping, later selected reuse and the exact remaining commit/purge callback order, followed by caller-held terminal munmap.

differential:child-managed-callback.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter child-member mi_manage_memory with caller-owned aligned memory: a failed metadata callback leaves a null arena output, unchanged errno, and retained mapping with one warning; retry publishes in the child's exact arena registry with the supplied callback and argument; selected Theap and allocation use the managed range; one purge callback returns no-recommit and later selected reuse follows the exact commit/purge trace; child destruction preserves the mapping until the caller's final munmap.

differential:public-reservation-warning.scope: Source-built pinned-C/native-adapter mi_reserve_os_memory_ex aligned OS map failure in the process main subprocess and a fresh child member: ENOMEM return, cleared arena output, errno from the failing primitive, ordered direct-map, aligned-fallback, and over-allocation warnings, and joined child teardown.

differential:subprocess-lifecycle.scope: Pinned-C/Rust root-child subprocess create/add-thread/visit/statistics/destroy traces: list order and sequence, child main Heap and metadata Theap membership, first child arena, refusal of a thread already in the main subprocess, a fresh thread's admission, allocation, and thread-done statistics, Heap visitation with early stop, the destroy-time statistics merge, destruction with a live metadata block, and the page handoff of a thread that finishes with live blocks (mapped abandonment and abandoned counts, a non-reclaiming free that keeps a page abandoned, one that releases it, and destruction with a live abandoned block).

fault:heap-lifecycle.scope: Deterministic failure injection for Heap, Theap, TLD, TLS-slot, arena-page metadata, and arena allocation with unique-owner audit.

unit:heap-membership.scope: Exact fresh-process Rust regressions for null, foreign, interior, non-main, and moved-page Heap queries and for quiescent non-head page utilization after a joined remote free.

unit:heap-statistics-visitation.scope: Focused Rust Heap statistics and visitation regressions.

unit:arena.scope: Focused Rust arena and managed-memory regressions.

upstream:test-api-heaps.scope: Unmodified test-api.c heap-os1, heap-os2, heap-many, and arena_reserve.

gates.acceptance: First-class Heaps follow src/heap.c: parent-main-Heap-allocated Heap images with a dynamic thread-local slot and subprocess list/count membership, lazy per-thread Theap creation, main-Heap delete/destroy refusal warnings, `mi_heap_delete` moving live pages to the main Heap as abandoned pages, `mi_heap_destroy` releasing every page, and exclusive-arena binding.
blocked_by: Non-main Heaps exist for threads of the process main subprocess (`subproc::main_heaps`, exported as mi_heap_new/mi_heap_main/mi_heap_delete/mi_heap_destroy/mi_heap_collect) and of child subprocesses (`types::heap_registry::lifecycle`). Process-main and child-subprocess mi_heap_theap have bounded source-built evidence. Heaps selected from one live exclusive parent have source-built allocation, delete, destroy, and failure traces in both subprocesses. A deleted process-main Heap's remote final free matches pinned C in both owner-exit orders. Deleting a worker-created Heap after that owner exits matches pinned C for regular and aligned singleton pages through page movement, remote final free, and collection. Destroying a Heap used by two exited workers matches pinned C for regular and aligned live pages. Source-built destroy and delete now also cover a still-attached second worker after creator exit, and thirty-two 64-round processes race worker exit with destruction. mi_heap_set_numa_affinity, deterministic lock-contention overlap, and failure coverage remain unproved or absent.

gates.acceptance: Pointer-to-Heap queries follow the source safe PageMap lookup and page Heap identity, including null, foreign, interior, main-Heap default, and moved-page results.
blocked_by: All five public Heap membership and region queries are exported. Selected null, foreign, interior, main/default, non-main, child, and moved-page lookups match pinned C; the quiescent utilization query also matches the source's non-head, fully committed page threshold after a joined remote free is collected. Exact fresh-process Rust regressions cover these live and moved-page boundaries; broader pointer and concurrent page-lifetime coverage remain open.

gates.acceptance: Every Heap-scoped allocation entry resolves the calling thread's Theap for that Heap (`_mi_heap_theap_get_or_init`) and then follows the same M4 allocation, zeroing, overflow, alignment, reallocation, string, and C++ new-handler semantics as the default-Heap entry points.
blocked_by: Every Heap-scoped allocation entry is exported for main-subprocess threads and follows its source path through the Heap's Theap; selected child-subprocess plain, zeroing, aligned through 128 MiB, owned-block, and same-child cross-Heap paths match pinned C, including the 256 MiB alignment refusal. Public aligned-at zeroing, offsets, failure errno, and one OS-backed live block across Heap deletion now have a direct differential. The required Heap allocation unit runner and complete per-entry failure and lifetime coverage remain open.

gates.acceptance: Heap statistics merge Theap statistics into their Heap and subprocess exactly as source, and Heap visitation walks the Heap's per-arena page bitmaps, abandoned bitmaps, and OS abandoned list with source area images and early-stop results. M7 separately owns the process-wide statistics, visitation, and output machinery these entries share.
blocked_by: mi_heap_visit_blocks is exported for quiescent non-main and process-main Heaps of the main subprocess. The shared adapter covers regular-before-OS singleton order, live-block and freed-block filtering, and area/block early stops. A clean-process differential covers exact main-Heap area/block populations through 1 to 1000 non-main Heaps and detached metadata collection. A two-owner mixed-workload differential covers accumulated main-Heap page population and release after both worker owners exit, Heap deletion and destruction, remote final frees, and collection. mi_heap_visit_abandoned_blocks is source-differentiated for worker-abandoned regular and OS singleton pages on a non-main Heap; process-main fixtures cover a selected regular bitmap page against a non-abandoned same-size page, live OS-list order, and a bounded combination of two regular bins and OS pages with live main-thread regular controls. Pinned source places each live OS singleton on the abandoned list immediately. These fixtures cover freed-block and freed-page omission, area/block early stops, and null-Heap selection. Child-subprocess and full concurrent visitation, broader Heap statistics, and complete lifetime evidence remain open.

gates.acceptance: The pinned header-only Heap conveniences compile unchanged against the Heap entry points they expand to, with the destroying STL allocator's shared Heap lifetime preserved.
blocked_by: The conveniences expand only to Heap entry points that do not exist yet.

gates.acceptance: Theap entry points follow src/theap.c and src/alloc.c: default-Theap get/set with lazy thread initialization and uninitialized-Theap refusal, direct Theap allocation and collection, Theap statistics, the deprecated Theap visitor, and the guarded setters' selected-build no-op or sampling behavior.
blocked_by: Process-main mi_theap_get_default/set_default and direct mi_theap_malloc/zalloc have source-built evidence across main, worker, and fork contexts. A child thread has source-built evidence for direct non-main Theap allocation, default substitution/restoration on one TLD, ownership, cache preservation, oversized errno, and teardown. The remaining direct allocation variants, collection, statistics, visitation, guarded setters, and broader cross-thread lifetime cases are absent or unproved.

gates.acceptance: Arena identity, geometry queries, OS and huge-page reservation, exclusive arenas, and caller-managed memory follow src/arena.c and src/os.c for the calling subprocess, including commit-callback behavior, size/alignment refusal, containment, exclusive-Heap binding, and destruction with the owning subprocess.
blocked_by: Main and child public aligned OS map failures match the source return, null arena output, primitive errno, and ordered direct-map, fallback, and over-allocation warnings. Public managed OS memory has main and child selected-allocation, short-region warning/errno, child destruction, and caller-held unmap evidence. Main and child callback-managed memory match selected commit/purge geometry, failed metadata commit warning with retry, and a failed purge that leaves its span committed for reuse; main short-region refusal also matches. Public arena queries now match across reserved, managed, child, and 17 GiB split-parent backing. Other OS failure branches, managed-memory cleanup, callback reentrancy and broader child lifetime cases, huge-page reservation, and wider arena query combinations remain open.

gates.acceptance: Subprocesses follow src/subproc.c: parent-metadata creation with child main Heap and metadata Theap, registry membership, thread admission refusal for threads already in another subprocess, Heap visitation under the Heap-list lock, statistics merge on destruction, and `mi_subproc_destroy` destroying non-main Heaps, the child main Heap, and the child arenas in source order while refusing the process main subprocess.
blocked_by: mi_subproc_main, mi_subproc_current, mi_subproc_new, mi_subproc_destroy, mi_subproc_add_current_thread, and mi_subproc_visit_heaps are exported for root children of the process main subprocess; selected child non-main Heap allocation, zeroing, alignment, and reallocation paths match pinned C, while nested children, complete Heap entry and failure coverage, and subprocess statistics entries remain absent.

gates.acceptance: Heap delete/destroy, arena destruction, and subprocess destruction are correct under cross-thread lifetime: Heaps used by several threads, owner threads exiting before and after Heap deletion, concurrent thread termination during Theap detachment with source try-lock backoff, remote frees into moved pages, and failure behavior for Heap, Theap, TLD, TLS-slot, arena-page metadata, and arena allocation, each compared with the pinned C oracle.
blocked_by: A deleted process-main Heap's remote final free matches pinned C before and after its owner exits. A worker-created Heap deleted after its owner exits matches pinned C through regular and singleton page movement, remote frees, and collection. A Heap created by one worker and used by another after the creator exits matches pinned C when the main thread destroys its three live regular/aligned pages after both workers exit. New source-built traces cover delete and destroy while that second worker remains attached, plus thirty-two 64-round destruction versus worker-exit race processes with owner counts returning to baseline. The heap-destroy, arena-destroy, and subprocess-lifecycle differentials cover the main-Heap Theap-list pass, quiescent arena-group retirement, and quiescent root-child subprocess destruction; deterministic lock-contention overlap and broader failure-path differentials remain open.

gates.acceptance: Applicable unmodified upstream Heap and subprocess tests pass with only environment/name binding: test-api.c `heap-os1`, `heap-os2`, `heap-many`, and `arena_reserve`; test-stress-heaps.c; and test-stress-subprocs.c.
blocked_by: The native adapter binds the Heap and reservation entries test-api.c uses, whose checks pass; test-stress-heaps.c and test-stress-subprocs.c need the subprocess entries and the remaining Heap entries, which the adapter does not export.
